subject: Private offer: multi-division purchase & term options
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@enterpriseco.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@enterpriseco.com>
Cc: AWS Marketplace Rep <aws-marketplace@amazon.com>
Date: 2027-03-28T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Private offer: multi-division purchase & term options

Hi Samir / Procurement team,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, EnterpriseCo is evaluating a consolidated private offer that would cover two internal buyer groups: Core Platform (annual committed seats) and Analytics (burst usage + reserved seats). Key asks from your side were: 1) flexible term lengths per division, 2) a single purchase flow if possible, and 3) clear invoicing.

Attached is a first-pass pricing workbook (RDW_EnterpriseCo_pricing_v1.xlsx) with three scenarios: 12-month consolidated term, 36-month with a migration credit, and a hybrid where Analytics has month-to-month burst credits layered on top of a 12-month seat commitment. High-level notes: 
- We can represent the divisions as separate line items in a single private offer so you receive one consolidated invoice while keeping accounting separated internally.
- If you prefer separate POs per division we can also produce distinct private offers; that just requires separate buyer account IDs.
- For discounts we modeled a volume tier starting at 250k annual spend for the 36-month option.

Next steps I propose: please confirm (a) preferred term structure (one of the three scenarios), (b) the buyer account IDs for each division, and (c) whether Procurement wants separate POs or one consolidated PO. Once confirmed I will loop in Legal for a short SOW draft and start the AWS private offer flow.

Thanks — happy to jump on another quick call if helpful.

— Irene
Irene Choi | Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: RDW_EnterpriseCo_pricing_v1.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@enterpriseco.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@enterpriseco.com>, AWS Marketplace Rep <aws-marketplace@amazon.com>
Date: 2027-03-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer: multi-division purchase & term options

Irene, thanks for the options and the quick turnaround. A couple clarifying questions before we lock a scenario: 

1) Invoicing: Our finance team prefers a single invoice to our corporate billing entity (EnterpriseCo HQ) but we need the ability to allocate costs to the divisions internally. Does a single private offer with multiple line items accomplish both?
2) PO process: Procurement often requires separate POs for each cost center — if we go that route, will we need separate private offers in AWS or can one private offer reference multiple POs?
3) AWS flow: do you need our AWS buyer account IDs now? I can pull them but would rather confirm the preferred model first.

Also CC'ing Procurement who will own the PO decision. If helpful we can do a 30 minute call with Finance and Procurement tomorrow.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Director, Cloud Platform — EnterpriseCo
[Attachment: EnterpriseCo_procurement_requirements.pdf (pdf)]

From: AWS Marketplace Rep <aws-marketplace@amazon.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@enterpriseco.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@enterpriseco.com>
Date: 2027-03-30T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer: multi-division purchase & term options

Hi all — quick note from Marketplace side: we can support both models but need the following to proceed with a single private offer that invoices to one billing entity while attributing charges to multiple internal accounts: 
- Buyer account IDs for each cost center (these are the 12-digit AWS account numbers)
- A clear statement whether you want separate POs or a single PO referencing the consolidated offer (AWS prefers one PO mapped to the private offer; multiple POs may require multiple private offers).

I'll also include a DocuSign private offer template link if you want to sign after the offer is generated: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?env=na1&acct=0000-0000&po=1

If you decide to go with a single private offer, provide the buyer IDs and our seller team will generate a private offer with line-item breakdowns and invoice to EnterpriseCo HQ.

— AWS Marketplace Ops
[No attachments]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@enterpriseco.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@enterpriseco.com>, AWS Marketplace Rep <aws-marketplace@amazon.com>
Date: 2027-04-01T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer: multi-division purchase & term options

Looping in recommended approach from a commercial/ops perspective. Short version: go with a single private offer (one DocuSign / one AWS private-offer record) that contains multiple line-items mapping to each division. Benefits: single invoice to HQ, simpler renewals and consolidated reporting; still supports internal cost allocations.

Operational notes: 
- We will need the buyer AWS account IDs for mapping line items. If Procurement insists on separate external POs we can create child private offers but that typically slows the provisioning path.
- For the 36-month scenario we recommend including a 12-month migration credit so Analytics can test burst patterns in year 1 without paying for full 36 months immediately.
- Legal: see the brief redline guidance attached (legal_redline_guidance.docx) — it calls out minimal SOW language to preserve buyer billing and data segregation expectations.

Irene, if you can collect the buyer IDs we will draft the private offer and send to AWS for provisioning; Samir, happy to run through the accounting implications on a quick call.

— Aditya
Aditya Rao | Head of Sales Ops | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: legal_redline_guidance.docx (docx)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@enterpriseco.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@enterpriseco.com>, AWS Marketplace Rep <aws-marketplace@amazon.com>
Date: 2027-04-02T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer: multi-division purchase & term options

Thanks everyone — quick legal confirmation. We are comfortable proceeding with a single private offer containing multiple line items, subject to the following being captured in the SOW: 
1) Explicit line-item mapping by division (Core Platform vs Analytics) and corresponding buyer account IDs for charge allocation.
2) Two term options presented in the SOW: a 12-month standard term and a 36-month term with a 15% committed discount plus a one-time migration credit equal to 1 month of the Analytics committed seats.
3) Invoicing to EnterpriseCo HQ with internal cost allocation metadata retained for reporting; specify PO number(s) in the private offer metadata as needed.

Samir / Procurement: please provide the AWS buyer account IDs and confirm whether Procurement wants a single PO or separate POs per cost center. Once we have that, Irene/Aditya will finalize the offer and I will sign the SOW on Redwood's side.

Thanks — I'll be available for a brief call tomorrow morning to finalize language.

— Laura
Laura Bennett | Legal Counsel | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: RDW_private_offer_SOW_draft.pdf (pdf)]
